newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish bourse rallies but expected lower on Monday.
newsitem.headline: Polish bourse rallies but expected lower on Monday.

text.p: The Polish bourse rose on Friday with second-tier stocks leading the rally but analysts saw the market dipping on Monday following strong selling after price fixing and the decline of some issues in continuous trade.
"After the falls we had in the continuous trade and stocks trading below their fixing prices, falls are very likely on Monday," said Dariusz Szepieniec, an analyst at Bank Slaski brokerage.
Analysts said the growth of small-caps, regarded as small investors' main area of interest combined with mixed blue-chip performance, signalled possible falls next week.
They said the bourse's heavyweights, which seemed fairly valued, were unlikely to attract fresh capital in near-term.
Some said small issues could fall in profit-taking but others believed their growth might be extended next week.
The main market's WIG index rose 1.1 percent, to 17,704.0, and turnover rose 17.3 percent to 236.4 million zlotys on all three markets as 70 issues rose, six fell and 14 were flat.
Universal surged 9.3 percent in the main market's heaviest trade on hopes that a consortium it leads will buy a news-stand chain Ruch SA, traders said.
Continuous trade turnover amounted to 21.2 million zlotys with the WIG 20 index closing at 1,760.6 points, 0.7 percent lower than in regular trade.
